# TamarackDB

> DCB event store in Go, over HTTP, on SQLite

The whole documentation in one Markdown file: [llms-full.txt](https://tamarackdb.github.io/llms-full.txt)

## Quickstart

- [Quickstart](https://tamarackdb.github.io/docs/quickstart/): Run TamarackDB with Docker and try it with curl: write events in a transaction, read them back, and see a commit refused because its read is stale.

## Concepts

What TamarackDB is, and the ideas the rest of the documentation builds on: the mental model, transactions, events, the store ID, conditions, projections.

- [Overview](https://tamarackdb.github.io/docs/concepts/overview/): What TamarackDB is: a DCB event store in Go, over HTTP, on one SQLite file. What it holds, its scope, the terms used everywhere, and the RFC 2119 key words.
- [Mental model](https://tamarackdb.github.io/docs/concepts/mental-model/): A picture of the whole model: a board, a card cabinet, employees with notebooks, and a head clerk, to reason about concurrency without technical details.
- [Transactions](https://tamarackdb.github.io/docs/concepts/transactions/): How a transaction works: it lives in the server's memory, pairs each read of events with a write, and writes it all at once, or nothing, at commit.
- [Events](https://tamarackdb.github.io/docs/concepts/events/): What an event holds: type, identifiers and metadata as tags, an opaque payload, its Sequence Position, its time, and the limits on its size and tags.
- [Store ID](https://tamarackdb.github.io/docs/concepts/store-id/): The store ID names the history a database file holds. Where it appears, when it changes, and why a position is always a store ID with a Sequence Position.
- [Append Condition](https://tamarackdb.github.io/docs/concepts/append-condition/): How an Append Condition protects a decision: its shape, its edge cases, several conditions per write, what it doesn't cover, and TamarackDB's DCB compliance.
- [Projections](https://tamarackdb.github.io/docs/concepts/projections/): What a projection is, how versions keep two writes from overwriting each other, what a projection may use, and how to rebuild projections from events.

## HTTP API

The contract between TamarackDB and its clients: every endpoint of the HTTP API, with its request, its response, and the errors it can return.

- [Conventions](https://tamarackdb.github.io/docs/http-api/conventions/): What every endpoint of the TamarackDB HTTP API has in common: the endpoints, connecting, strict request bodies, the body size cap, and the store ID header.
- [Query grammar](https://tamarackdb.github.io/docs/http-api/query-grammar/): The query grammar used to read events and in Append Conditions: "all", "none", query items, the matching rules, and the size limits.
- [Reading events](https://tamarackdb.github.io/docs/http-api/read-events/): QUERY /events: reading committed events a page at a time, the NDJSON response and its trailer, cursor pagination, and resuming a page that was cut short.
- [Transactions](https://tamarackdb.github.io/docs/http-api/transactions/): The /tx endpoints: begin a transaction, read and write events, read and write projections, commit or abandon it, with each body, response, and error.
- [Writing](https://tamarackdb.github.io/docs/http-api/write/): POST /write: one write with events, Append Conditions, and projection changes, outside any transaction. Its limits, response, conflicts, and retries.
- [Projections](https://tamarackdb.github.io/docs/http-api/projections/): Reading one projection with GET /projections/{type}/{id}, its version header, and deleting projections in bulk, by type or all at once, for a rebuild.
- [Reset](https://tamarackdb.github.io/docs/http-api/reset/): POST /reset, in development mode only: empties the store and draws a new store ID, for tests. What happens to the writes queued before and after it.
- [Errors](https://tamarackdb.github.io/docs/http-api/errors/): The error envelope of the TamarackDB HTTP API, every error code with its status and meaning, and the causes of a 400 InvalidRequest response.
- [Example: an online store](https://tamarackdb.github.io/docs/http-api/example/): One order in an online store as the HTTP calls an application sends: five decisions and their projections in one transaction, then a projector with POST /write.

## Integration

Building on the TamarackDB HTTP API: what every client of the protocol must do, from positions and cut pages to transactions and lost responses.

- [Client libraries](https://tamarackdb.github.io/docs/integration/client-libraries/): What every client of the TamarackDB protocol must do: keep positions whole, spot a cut page, treat versions as opaque, handle transactions and lost responses.

## Operations

Running a TamarackDB instance: installing it, configuring it, securing it, checking its health, watching it, backing it up, and maintaining it.

- [Install](https://tamarackdb.github.io/docs/operations/install/): Getting a TamarackDB instance running: on your own machine with Docker, in production with systemd, from the binaries, or alongside an app in Docker.
- [Configuration](https://tamarackdb.github.io/docs/operations/configuration/): Every setting of tamarackdb-server: where settings come from, the full table of keys, environment variables, and defaults, and how to size the limits.
- [Security](https://tamarackdb.github.io/docs/operations/security/): Who can reach a TamarackDB instance and who can read its data: the unix socket, a reverse proxy for other hosts, the Bearer token, and file permissions.
- [Health check](https://tamarackdb.github.io/docs/operations/health-check/): GET /health: how a process supervisor or a load balancer checks that a TamarackDB instance responds and that its SQLite database can be reached.
- [Observability](https://tamarackdb.github.io/docs/operations/observability/): GET /stats: counters of writes, conflicts, transactions, and errors since the server started, and what each one tells about the instance and its clients.
- [Logs](https://tamarackdb.github.io/docs/operations/logs/): The access log of tamarackdb-server: one line per request, what it carries and never carries, logLevel, and the fixed level of each outcome.
- [Backup](https://tamarackdb.github.io/docs/operations/backup/): tamarackdb-backup keeps a standing copy of an instance's events: its settings, how a run works, local or remote sources, restoring, and scheduling.
- [Maintenance](https://tamarackdb.github.io/docs/operations/maintenance/): The two maintenance tasks left to you, both run by hand while the server is stopped: giving back disk space with VACUUM, and a full ANALYZE.
- [Development mode](https://tamarackdb.github.io/docs/operations/dev-mode/): What devMode turns on, POST /reset and Go's profiling endpoints, why it must stay off in production, and how to profile a request with pprof.
